text:
Chen: Heads-up — saw a burst of ECC/Xid alerts hitting paging for a handful of us-west nodes this morning. Lots of 1-2 count blips that still caused SLO noise. Thinking we need a smarter noise heuristic rather than nuking alerts on 1 count.
Alex: +1. I looked — most bursts are short-lived (under 3m) and concentrated on cards with similar firmware. Two ideas: 1) group alerts by gpu_device_id + pod_annotation so a single pod/card cluster doesn't multiply pages, 2) use a short-term rate threshold and require sustained increase before paging.
Jamie: Agree on grouping. Also want to throw in a "synthetic baseline" approach: compute expected 5m error distribution per card cohort (age/batch) and only promote alerts if increase is > p95 for that cohort. That avoids global static thresholds.
Sara: If we go cohorting we need tagging on the node/gpu object. We already have node labels for rack/region; can we add gpu_batch and fleet_age as annotations on the node or exporter?
Alex: Yeah either node annotations or dcgm-exporter relabel to add `gpu_batch`/`manufacture_year` from admin inventory. Then Prom rules can group by those labels.
Chen: Prototype Prom rule I sketched (open to edits):
```
alert: TransientECCBurst
expr: sum by (gpu_device_id, pod) ( increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[5m]) )
  > 3
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: warning
annotations:
  summary: "Transient ECC burst on {{ $labels.gpu_device_id }} (pod={{ $labels.pod }})"
```
This groups and requires 3m sustained. Might still be noisy but better than immediate page.
infra-bot: Note: last week we lowered the debounce window from 5m->1m for faster detection; that change increased churn across the cluster (see #1748801234). Reverting made pages drop by ~30%.
alerts-bot: Created ticket INF-4721 to track cohort baseline work and rule PR.
Jamie: For the cohort baseline, I propose a nightly sweep job that computes per-card percentiles for `increase(...[5m])` over 24h and writes recording rules like `dcgm_ecc_error_5m_p95{gpu_batch="X"}`. Then alert uses `> dcgm_ecc_error_5m_p95{gpu_batch=~"$batch"} * 1.5` to detect regressions.
Sara: I'll spin up the sweep job tomorrow in staging. Quick adhoc to validate counts: `kubectl exec -n monitoring -c prom-query prom-query-0 -- promql "sum by(gpu_device_id)(increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m]))"`
Alex: If sweep looks good I can open the Prometheus rule PR to: add grouping, replace absolute threshold with cohort p95 multiplier, and add a recording rule `record: dcgm_ecc_error_5m:rate`. Will also add `for: 3m` and reduce page severity for single-pod hits.
Chen: Action items: Sara -> run sweep + dump cohort stats (by EOD tomorrow). Alex -> draft PR for rule and recording rules. Jamie -> write short doc describing cohort labeling and how to update inventory. I'll add node annotation task to infra backlog for GPU batch tagging.
Sara: ack. I'll post results in this thread once sweep completes. :thumbsup:
Alex: thanks — also let's add a brief runbook snippet to the rule annotation on how oncall should interpret grouped alerts (eg check `gpu_batch`, `kernel` and `recent driver update`).
Chen: Perfect. We're avoiding a bunch of churn and also getting data to do smarter long-term triage.
infra-bot: Reminder: any change to alerting needs a test window and rollback plan. See playbook `alerting-change-process.md`.
alerts-bot: INF-4721 updated: assignees Sara, Alex; target: 72h.
